sources.entry: Jellyfin - Media server for audio, video, books, comics, and photos with a sleek interface and robust transcoding capabilities. Almost all modern platforms have clients, including Roku, Android TV, iOS, and Kodi. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) GPL-2.0 C#/deb/Docker
Jellyfin - The Free Software Media System. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://jellyfin.org) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Jellyfin is a free, open-source media server (C#/.NET) that streams audio, video, books, comics, and photos from a dedicated server to client apps on other devices.
summary.what_it_does: Jellyfin is a self-hosted media system that serves audio, video, books, comics, and photos from a central server to end-user devices through multiple apps. The README describes it as an alternative to the proprietary Emby and Plex, and says it was descended from Emby's 3.5.2 release and ported to .NET for cross-platform support. This repository holds only the backend server code; the web client is a separate project that the server can host. The README covers building from source, running via dotnet or an IDE, running in GitHub Codespaces, running tests, and hosting the web client separately. Setup requires the .NET 10 SDK and ffmpeg. The README notes that FreeBSD is not yet supported, and the setup wizard is unavailable when the web client is hosted separately.
use_cases: Stream personal movies and TV shows to devices on my home network
Host a self-hosted music library for streaming
Serve photos and comics from a home server
Replace a proprietary Plex or Emby media server
Develop or contribute to the Jellyfin server codebase
Run a media server from source with dotnet
how_to_run: git clone the repository (see README for the URL)
Obtain the jellyfin-web client files (build from jellyfin-web or copy from an existing install)
Alternatively: dotnet build, then run the Jellyfin.Server executable from its build output directory
notable: Descended from Emby 3.5.2 and ported to .NET for cross-platform support
Free software with no premium licenses or paid features, per the README
Server can host the web client itself, or the client can be hosted separately with a nowebclient flag
Includes Codespaces dev container configurations and launch profiles for Visual Studio and VS Code
Translation support through a Weblate instance
caveats: Not supported on FreeBSD, per the README
The web client is not included and must be obtained separately before the server can serve a UI
The setup wizard cannot run when the web client is hosted separately
